events.body:
Nice finding, Concept ACK

> None of the existing tests put a labeled output past the first batch

There is [one BIP-352 test vector](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/2b4a7b906f1da8c4592ab5562faddac971327fbc/src/modules/silentpayments/bip352_send_and_receive_test_vectors.json#L3324) where 2323 tx outputs are labeled matches and findings in higher batches (j_start > 0) occur, so an incorrect tx output index calculation with the mutant patch in the PR description is at least already exercised. But it unfortunately remains undetected, as the checking is not very thorough for this one, [only the number of found outputs is verified and nothing else](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/2b4a7b906f1da8c4592ab5562faddac971327fbc/src/modules/silentpayments/tests_impl.h#L909). Maybe we could do something like "if there are N matches, ensure that those are all with different output x-only pubkeys". This would have caught this issue I think, as with the mutant patch several matches map to the same tx outputs. Ideas welcome (could be in a different PR though).

I opened PR https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1950 and confirmed that the [suggested](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1943#issuecomment-5902032203) new check on test vectors of silent payments does capture the mutant described here. 

Is this PR still necessary? This one checks for exacts outputs and is more explicit about testing the even and the odd candidate slots because it scans with p and -p.

> Is this PR still necessary? This one checks for exacts outputs and is more explicit about testing the even and the odd candidate slots because it scans with p and -p.

I think it makes sense to keep this PR as well, explicitly verifying outputs and exercising both y-parities are useful additions. I didn't try, but I suppose it would be possible to come up with a mutant patch that's caught by this PR, but not by #1950.

Tested on 0f03931.

I think this is still very much needed on top of #1950. The check added in #1950 only asserts pairwise uniqueness across found outputs in the 2323 vector (`full_check = 0`), which doesn't check against expected ground-truth pubkeys or labels. If a transaction has filler outputs and only a single match in higher batches (exactly what this test sets up with `LABEL_BATCH_SIZE` fillers), the uniqueness check is trivially satisfied and wouldn't catch an incorrect index mapping to a filler.

On top of that, explicitly exercising both even and odd candidate slots (p and -p) past batch 0 is great to have.

One minor suggestion: in `test_recipient_scan_label_precedes_direct_match`, `f[0].label` is also verified against the cache via `secp256k1_silentpayments_recipient_label_serialize`. Adding that check here would also ensure `label_ge` itself is verified for both parities beyond batch 0.

> One minor suggestion: in `test_recipient_scan_label_precedes_direct_match`, `f[0].label` is also verified against the cache via `secp256k1_silentpayments_recipient_label_serialize`. Adding that check here would also ensure `label_ge` itself is verified for both parities beyond batch 0.

`label_ge` is read from the current batch's candidate array at the in-batch position `i`, so it's the same code path for every batch and parities. Only the returned index depends on `j_start`:

```c
*label_ge = label_candidates_ge[i];
return (int)(j_start + i / 2);
```

I'll keep this test focused on the output index mapping.

events.body:
Thanks for the review! Force-pushed 0c3c70d5f70d09bddf3e9ed5247d382ebe8d577e updating the test so it covers every position mapping across multiple label batches, which kills the mutant suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1943#issuecomment-6078211325.

Note that a test can't feasibly kill every possible mutant: one can always be crafted to misbehave only on input sizes beyond those tested, and exhaustively covering all output counts and positions is impractical. This test targets the realistic mapping errors instead.
